# Omaha (PLO): what’s different from Hold'em

*Four hole cards, the exactly-two-plus-three rule that trips up every new player, and how to work out a pot-sized bet.*

3 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

Pot-Limit Omaha — **PLO** — is the second most popular game in home games. The blinds, the button, the four betting rounds and the hand rankings are all the same as Hold'em. Three things change.

## 1. You get four hole cards

Everyone is dealt **four** cards face down instead of two. More cards means more possible hands, so strong hands are much more common. A pair that would be good in Hold'em is often nowhere near the best hand in Omaha.

> **A strong starting hand:** `A♠ A♥ K♠ Q♥`
>
> Two aces, both suited to another card, plus high cards that connect.

## 2. Exactly two from your hand, exactly three from the board

This is the rule that catches everyone. Your five-card hand must use **exactly two** of your hole cards and **exactly three** board cards. Not one, not three, not four.

> **No flush:** `A♥ K♥ 7♥ 2♥` · Board: `Q♥ 9♣ 5♦ J♠ 3♠`
>
> Four hearts in your hand, but only one on the board. You can use only two hearts from your hand, so you have no flush — just ace high.

> **Still no flush:** `A♠ Q♦ J♣ 8♥` · Board: `K♠ 9♠ 6♠ 2♠ 4♦`
>
> Four spades on the board, but you hold only one. You need two spades in your hand.

> **Full house:** `K♣ K♦ 7♠ 4♥` · Board: `8♣ 8♦ 8♥ Q♠ 3♠`
>
> Your two kings plus the three eights: eights full of kings. With only one king you’d have just three eights — you always need two of your own cards to play.

> **Tip — How to read your hand:** Pick every pair of cards from your hand (there are six pairs) and try each one with the board. The best of those is your hand.

## 3. Bets are capped at the size of the pot

PLO is almost always played **pot-limit**. You can bet anything from the big blind up to the pot. To raise, the most you can raise to is: call first, then add the size of the pot after your call.

| Step | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Pot before the bet | 100 |
| Opponent bets | 50 (pot is now 150) |
| Your call would make the pot | 150 + 50 = 200 |
| Your maximum raise is to | 50 + 200 = 250 |

> **Tip — Shortcut:** Maximum raise to = 3 × the last bet + everything in the pot before it. Here: 3 × 50 + 100 = 250. Preflop with blinds 1/2, a pot-sized opening raise is to 7.

## What changes in play

- **Winning hands are bigger.** Two pair and sets often lose; straights, flushes and full houses win.
- **Aim for the nuts.** A flush that isn’t the ace-high flush is in danger.
- **Draws are strong.** A hand with many outs can be the favourite even against a made hand, so equities run closer than in Hold'em.
- **Watch the pairs on the board.** When the board pairs, a full house becomes possible.

> **Note — Five-card PLO:** Some groups play with five hole cards. The rule doesn’t change: exactly two from your hand, three from the board.
